messages:
Alex: ok team — I want to lock a short playbook for how we surface failures across chat/completions, embeddings, rerank, and tool calls. customer asks are piling up, need clear launch gates.
Deepa: +1. can we scope to three classes: client (4xx), transient (429/503), permanent server (5xx)?
Morgan: that maps to infra signals. question: do we separate model-unavailable (e.g., model cold start/capacity) from generic 503? customers want distinct handling.
Sanjay: customers ask for explicit "model_unavailable" vs "rate_limited" to show in UI. They want different retry guidance.
Jamie: docs + SDK changes need concrete codes and header contract. small change window preferred for launch.
Alex: proposal: 1) Validation/client: 400 + subcode header (x-rw-subcode) for structured UI hints. 2) Rate limits: 429 with Retry-After and x-rw-quota-type (global|model|customer). 3) Model unavailable: 503 with x-rw-retry-type=warmup|fallback and optional backoff_hint. 4) Internal errors: 500 with correlation id.
Deepa: I like structured headers. instead of x-rw-subcode maybe use x-rw-error-code to avoid mixing. also SDK should expose high-level enums not raw codes.
Morgan: operationally we can emit metrics for each header value. for model_unavailable we can include prometheus label model_unavailable=1.
Jamie: example header snippets for docs: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 10
X-RW-Quota-Type: model
X-RW-Error-Code: rate_limit_model
```
Sanjay: customer feedback: some enterprise customers want 429 broken into soft (throttle) vs hard (quota exhausted). can we add `quota_mode` values soft|hard?
Alex: yes add `quota_mode` as optional header. initial list: quota_mode in {soft,hard}, quota_type in {global,model,customer}.
Deepa: SDK behavior: on 429 with quota_mode=soft -> auto-retry with exponential backoff and jitter (configurable). on quota_mode=hard -> surface to app, no auto-retry. need tests.
Morgan: for 503 model_unavailable, we should support graceful fallback routing: if request has fallback_model in request metadata, runtime will attempt fallback and return 200 + x-rw-fallback-used header. else return 503 with backoff_hint seconds.
Jamie: add clear launch criteria: docs published + SDK mapping + infra emits metrics + 2-day canary + regression tests for retries and header propagation.
Alex: can we summarize acceptance criteria? I propose: 
- Spec PR merged with code samples and header list
- SDKs (py/node/go) map errors into exceptions/enums and respect quota_mode
- Runtime implements headers for 429/503/5xx and emits metrics
- E2E tests: simulate rate limit, simulate model down, verify client/backoff behavior
- Canary: 48h with canary flag and telemetry review
If all green -> ship.
Deepa: timeline ask: engineering needs 3 weeks to implement headers + tests, +1 week SDK changes, +1 week docs/canary -> 5 weeks. feasible?
Alex: sounds good. prioritize the header contract first so SDK/docs can start in parallel.
Morgan: ops note: we must ensure Retry-After semantics are in seconds and monotonic. also add x-rw-retry-after-ms for clients that want ms precision.
Sanjay: I'll coordinate enterprise customers and flag any blockers; prefer a beta opt-in for them.
Jamie: I'll draft the spec doc and example snippets, + a sample UI mapping table for SREs and CS. will share PR by EOD tomorrow.
Deepa: one more: propose adding a machine-friendly error body with fields `error_code`, `message`, `retry_after_ms` so non-header consumers can still programmatically act. keep headers as primary contract.
Alex: agree. final ask: include a short compatibility note: old clients that only see 500/429 should degrade gracefully to generic retry logic. add a deprecation plan for any changes to existing headers.
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled to canary cluster at 2026-04-07T09:00Z for feature/err-codes.
Alex: thanks all — next step: Jamie PR, Deepa infra tickets, SDK owners looped. small incremental rollout, full launch after canary and customer signoff. :thumbsup:
